A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 46 pages of v1 and 52 pages of v2, including figures, equations, references, and proof appendices, support comparison; moved and repeated material can be matched.

before.justification: Figures 1–3 report original simulations of matrix PCA and single-index learning, including comparisons of SGD, SGD-M, and SGD-U.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation results in Figures 1–3. Their retention qualifies despite the revision concentrating on theory.

M1.justification: v1 treats momentum and scalar-preconditioned SGD separately, with Section 2.1 specifying the latter for beta = 0. v2 Appendix 5 additionally specifies their joint update, applying scalar Markovian preconditioning inside the momentum recursion. The algorithms used in the simulations remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The evaluated coverage remains matrix PCA and single-index models with the same polynomial link functions and noise scenarios. The added phase-retrieval diffusion theorem and cited classification applications do not introduce new evaluations.

E2.justification: Figures 1–2 retain SGD, SGD-U, and SGD-M with beta = 0.5 and 0.9. Figure 3 retains SGD versus SGD-U. Newly cited methods are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The simulations retain n = 10,000, the same signal and noise settings, alignment statistics, and step-size selection. The stated horizons remain 20n steps in Figure 1, 6n in Figure 2, and one million in Figure 3.

E4.justification: The existing comparisons across signal strength, momentum, noise, and link functions are retained without new empirical ablations or robustness tests. The added diffusion analysis is a mathematical derivation, assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same reference to independent runs without adding repetition counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new diffusion covariance expressions concern theoretical dynamics rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Reported analytical outcomes are corrected: Proposition 3.9 changes the fixed-point value of r² from c_delta/(2 sqrt(2/pi)) to pi c_delta²/8, and the expression following Proposition 3.4 changes numerical diffusion-limit prefactors. Figures 1–3 and their empirical findings remain identical; these are corrected predictions, not measured performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds Definitions 5.1–5.2 and Theorem 5.3 for jointly preconditioned momentum, plus Theorem 8.1 and Proposition 3.12 for single-index diffusion limits. It also restricts the cross-sample localizability condition to beta > 0, revises tensor-PCA bounds, supplies an explicit single-index localizability argument, and corrects existing formulas. These materially expand and revise the theoretical treatment.

C1.justification: The abstract remains substantively identical. The central claims remain momentum–SGD equivalence after suitable rescaling and the stability, fixed-point, and admissible-step-size benefits of normalized gradients on the same two model families. The revised contributions and new conclusion elaborate these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds discussion of applicability beyond conventional smoothness and convexity assumptions. Section 3.2.2 interprets the new phase-retrieval diffusion limit through equatorial instability when r² < 1, while the conclusion identifies broader scalar and matrix preconditioning as future directions.

D1.justification: The simulation settings and procedural disclosures are unchanged. No implementation instructions, hardware information, computational budgets, or code/data access information are added; the expanded technical material concerns mathematical assumptions and proofs.

R1.justification: The introduction adds positioning around dimension-scaled momentum and gradient clipping, including Ferbach et al. and Marshall et al., and removes the heavy-tailed continuous-limit discussion and Simsekli et al. reference. The central positioning as an extension of the existing effective-dynamics framework remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and contributions receive localized rewrites, a conclusion is added, and notation and appendix references are revised. Appendix 8.5 repeats existing even-monomial propositions under new numbers. Most existing exposition and proofs retain their structure.

P2.justification: All three figure images and captions are unchanged. Figures 1–2 move relative to surrounding text, and added sections cause local equation and paragraph reflow. The overall single-column layout and plot designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects existing formulas, makes preconditioning assumptions explicit, and expands the proofs. However, the newly added phase-retrieval result is internally inconsistent: Equation (14) gives the c_delta correction in dr² the opposite sign from Theorem 8.1, Equation (21), and its specialization. The improvements in precision and coverage coexist with an unresolved correctness issue, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
